entries.title: Bloemgracht: the townsman, the farmer and the sailor
entries.reason: 87-91 are listed: check no monument draft covers them
entries.hook: Three identical gables, three stones: not trades but three ways of living in the Golden Age.

entries.title: Marnixstraat 291-293, houses on the old bastion below the street
entries.hook: Houses already on the 1625 map sit below street level, with bastion stones along their sunken lane.

entries.title: Het Gangenproject, the Willemsstraat's vanished alleys in the pavement
entries.hook: Tiles mark the 57 slum alleys of the filled Goudsbloemgracht; the Jordaanmuseum fought nine years to lay them.

entries.title: Vaste klant, a statue paid for a bar tab
entries.hook: A young artist settled his café tab with a statue of a sad regular stroking the cat.

entries.title: Energie en tijd, Verhulst on the substation
entries.hook: A 1962 concrete-and-steel relief on the biggest substation of its day, where the English gasworks stood.

entries.title: Theo Thijssen Museum
entries.hook: The writer's birth house, rebuilt in its old form after a fuss, with a small museum of the 1890 Jordaan.

entries.title: Lindengracht, the filled canal and the eel riot
entries.hook: Police stopped an eel-pulling game here in 1886; the riot that followed left 26 dead.

entries.title: The anonymous sculptor of the Anjeliersstraat
entries.reason: how many remain needs a walk
entries.hook: Small iron figures appear on Jordaan walls overnight; the maker stays anonymous, rumour once said Queen Beatrix.

entries.title: Kees de jongen on the "Tuinpleintje"
entries.hook: Theo Thijssen's schoolboy painted on a Tuinstraat wall in 2025, paid by residents' vote; pupils sang at the unveiling.

entries.title: Bevrijdingslinde van Jordaankinderen
entries.reason: pin approximate; urn under the tree unconfirmed
entries.hook: A lime paid by pupils of thirteen schools in 1946 for war-dead Jordaan children; neighbours saved it twice.

entries.title: Noordermarkt: what the locals point at
entries.reason: Noorderkerk draft (jordaan-3) already has the Jordaanoproer statue as a Look for line: keep the church story there
entries.hook: The stolen strike plaque found in an alley, a dune-water tap post, and markets that fought "vertrutting".

entries.title: Johnny Jordaanplein, the people's statue garden
entries.reason: well known to Amsterdammers: pitch the self-management
entries.hook: Busts of Jordaan singers on a square the council never named; a self-appointed keeper nailed up the sign.

entries.title: Eerste Marnixplantsoen, the bastion in the grass and the 1966 riot
entries.hook: The Singelgracht's only bastion still pointed; the 1966 builders' riot began at the patronaat at no. 1.

entries.title: Noorderspeeltuin on the Carthusian graveyard
entries.reason: burial is "vermoedelijk"; Karthuizerhof draft names the graveyard
entries.hook: The Jordaan's oldest club (1908), pointed-roof huts and majorettes on the graveyard where Jan Klaassen may lie.

entries.title: Nassaubioscoop, the Moorish front on the Lijnbaansgracht
entries.hook: A 1913 cinema's three horseshoe arches, behind netting for years; the Jordaanmuseum wanted it and lost.

entries.title: Perlee, the street organ workshop
entries.hook: Street organs rented "with a monkey" since 1875; at Westerstraat 119 since 1932, still making organ books.

entries.title: Marnixplein: the Volksvrouw and Krop's lost bather
entries.reason: Volksvrouw's exact spot to check (Okay half)
entries.hook: A communist sculptor's wife in bronze, and Krop's bather lost "by miscommunication" when the baths came down, back 2019.

entries.title: Palmgracht: the cauliflower stone and the cake-slice school
entries.hook: DE BLOMKOOL was a pun on the neighbours named Cool; at no. 74 a wedge school once stood on two canals.

entries.title: Hermanusje van Alles, the drugstore of window puns
entries.reason: single source for the facts; shop (borderline)
entries.hook: A drugstore since 1973 with old stock and fifty years of window puns, now a book.

entries.title: Electric Ladyland
entries.hook: Nick Padalino's fluorescent cave, built over seven years, where visitors push the buttons.

entries.title: Joost Swarte's "Parels van de Jordaan", Willemsstraat 204
entries.reason: are the stairwell charms visible from the street?
entries.hook: A cartoonist's 2010 housing block, called a monument-in-the-making and a "shocking intrusion" in one issue.

entries.title: Tweede Marnixplantsoen, Naatje who came home
entries.hook: A little statue evicted from the Rokin by the metro, parked here "temporarily" since 2008, and a poem stair.

entries.title: Lauriergracht 12, the last tile bakery
entries.reason: Okay; not open; scout says merge with 3221 but no draft carries that number
entries.hook: Two and a half centuries of tile baking behind a passage with a hardstone gutter for wheelbarrows.

entries.title: Broenshofje, six rooms off a corridor
entries.hook: An 1851 hofje of six rooms for Protestant single women, with a party parcel at Sinterklaas.

entries.title: Westerstraat 202, a soap boiler's stone in a 1980s wall
entries.hook: A 1770 stone from the soap works that paid for a country house, set in a 1986 new-build.

entries.title: Blijvend Applaus, Wim Sonneveld's houses for old artists
entries.reason: Okay; single source; house numbers to check
entries.hook: The comedian's foundation gives retired artists cheap homes; his gable stone over the door.

entries.title: Bloemgracht 76, Blaeu's printing house
entries.reason: Okay; single source, check against a Blaeu source
entries.hook: Site of the Blaeu map printers on the Bloemgracht.

entries.title: Gedenksteen Bloemgracht 82
entries.reason: Okay; single source (Wijkkrant); plaque on a private house
entries.hook: Resistance arms store where three men died weeks before liberation; a resident now opens it as an "Open Verzetshuis".

entries.title: Delverssteeg and the Sevenhuysengangh
entries.hook: A door at Elandsgracht 114 led for four centuries into a covered alley of c. 1614 to nine tiny houses.

entries.title: Looiersplantsoen, the toddlers' square run by neighbours
entries.hook: Three residents have run this toddlers' square since 1994: fourteen sandpit fills, forty brooms, one pair of clogs.

entries.title: The phone box library, Boomstraat
entries.hook: A 1933-type phone box, won by residents' vote, now the street's book exchange: "not for the IKEA guide of 2004".

entries.title: De Reus van Bickerseiland
entries.hook: A wooden Roman soldier taken to Alicante in 1972, traced by islanders to Canada, home again in 2009.

entries.title: The oldest wild fig of Amsterdam, Drieharingenbrug
entries.hook: Nobody planted it: a fig seeded itself into the quay wall around 1990 and now bears fruit.

entries.title: Haarlemmer Houttuinen: the motorway that stopped at a bridge
entries.reason: replacement plan of the bridge to check
entries.hook: A car bridge built for a motorway that never came, painted by one of Europe's first women graffiti writers.

entries.title: "De walvis" and the poem on the quay, Hollandse Tuin
entries.hook: A granite fountain-sculpture islanders call the whale, and a neighbour's poem cut into the quay wall.

entries.title: Tuin Bickersgracht Noordkop and De Dierencapel
entries.reason: pin approximate; tree-felling plan outcome unknown
entries.hook: A neighbour-kept garden reserve with bird islands at the island's tip, beside the children's farm saved in 2006.

entries.title: Kunstroute Nieuwe Houttuinen
entries.hook: One resident turned "a road from nowhere to nowhere" into an art route: Jonas and the whale, eye-twisting underpasses.

entries.title: Jacob van Lennep and the first water tap
entries.hook: A steel-and-glass statue twelve years after its fountain fell through, where the city's first dune water was sold.

entries.title: Door wind bewogen beweging (Wicher Meursing)
entries.hook: Friends built the designer's wind sculpture from his model after his death; it swings or stands dead still.

entries.title: De Roode Bioscoop, the anarchists' cinema
entries.reason: outcome of the 2024 name case unknown (Under threat)
entries.hook: An anarchist's 1913 cinema "to spread red ideas", now a volunteer stage fighting its landlord over the name.

entries.title: Prinseneiland: the last walwindas, the Palmentuin and Mandela's garden
entries.reason: winch spot and garden access to check; mural maker unknown
entries.hook: The city's last shore-winch cover for tar barrels, a neighbour-made garden, and a mural of Mandela's prison garden.

entries.title: De Aardige Amsterdammer, Droogbak
entries.hook: An outstretched hand for the volunteers who help the homeless; stolen on King's Day 2015, remade.

entries.title: Zandhoek: the Oranjeboom and Stadsherstel's first house
entries.reason: which tree needs a site check; single source for the tree
entries.hook: Wilhelmina's 1898 lime behind its small fence, and De Keijser, the first house Stadsherstel restored (1959).

entries.title: De Mof and the widow called Sluys, Haarlemmerdijk 109
entries.reason: shop (borderline); the name is a wartime slur, careful copy
entries.hook: Neighbours nicknamed a German workwear seller "de mof" in 1885; the SLUYS stone above names a widow, not a town.

entries.title: Vinkenstraat, a wall that makes you see suns
entries.hook: Stare at Roland Schimmel's black circles and coloured after-images appear; a folded-steel square a few steps on.

entries.title: Wubboboom, Haarlemmerplein
entries.reason: Okay; or a Look for line in Willem Drees's birthplace (same square)
entries.hook: An elm for astronaut Wubbo Ockels with benches quoting "we are all astronauts of Spaceship Earth".

entries.title: De Oude Amsterdammer, Korte Prinsengracht 5
entries.hook: A corner house whose shopfront with two doors still shows the old bar.

entries.title: Stones that came home, Bickersgracht 14 and 22
entries.hook: A vanished 1664 gable stone turned up in a dentist's wall in Moordrecht and was bricked back in.

entries.title: Toon Ylandplantsoen, "ons klein Keukenhof"
entries.hook: An orphaned strip turned neighbours' garden, named in 2016 behind its gardener's back after him.

entries.title: Het Groene Hoofd aan het IJ
entries.reason: Okay; single source; or a Look for line in Rederij Goedkoop
entries.hook: Two residents turned a tug firm's concrete mooring platform into planters and benches, shovelling the grit themselves.

entries.title: Gables that swim: Abraham Zeeman's sea fish and De Hond's dolphins
entries.hook: A man named Seaman had his gable claws carved as sea fish around 1715.

entries.title: De Groote Keijser, the squat that became a fortress
entries.hook: Squatters turned six canal houses into a fortress in 1978; the mayor refused to send the police.

entries.title: The gaper of Het Heertje, now "O Johnny"
entries.hook: A stolen drugstore gaper, a replica removed in a 2020 racism row, then a two-faced Medusa gaper.

entries.title: Reestraat 6, Anton de Kom's Amsterdam house
entries.reason: dates of his stay differ; plaque unconfirmed
entries.hook: The anti-colonial writer of "Wij slaven van Suriname" lived here in 1935; Stadsherstel saved the near-ruin.

entries.title: Brouwersgracht stones: a bag of coins and a cowherd who stayed home
entries.hook: A money bag that "won't give to friends", dated 1772, and other stones Stadsherstel rescued.

entries.title: De Poezenboot
entries.hook: A woman took in one cat and kittens in 1966; now a purpose-built ark, still a working shelter.

entries.title: Descartes at Westermarkt 6
entries.reason: beside A-list Westerkerk; second source to find
entries.hook: Descartes lived here in 1634 and fathered a daughter with the housekeeper; a pavement tile says "Ik denk, dus ik ben".

entries.title: Zuid-Afrikahuis and the "boekverdrinking"
entries.hook: Europe's largest library on South Africa, where masked activists threw books into the canal in 1984.

entries.title: The Heerenlogement gate on the Keizersgracht
entries.hook: The gate of "the noblest taverne in the world" was carried here by its last auctioneer when the inn fell in 1874.

entries.title: The Knobbeliep: Amsterdam's own knobbly elms, Westermarkt and Nieuwe Herengracht
entries.hook: An undescribed elm cultivar with a burred trunk; only five are known, one an 1891 veteran on the Nieuwe Herengracht.

entries.title: The thickest tree in Centrum, a plane at Molenpad 2
entries.reason: or a Look for in the Molenpad draft (gg-west-3)
entries.hook: An oriental plane 5.75 m round, planted for a bank around 1860.

entries.title: Bergstraat: De Naaister and the corn measurer who came home
entries.reason: no second source; statue's house number and date unclear
entries.hook: Residents' own bronze seamstress, and a 1608 gable stone found in another building's hall and brought back.

entries.title: Klipper Bestevaer at the head of the Keizersgracht
entries.hook: A 1906 clipper lived in as a home; a storm-felled elm snapped both masts in 2023, neighbours rallied.

entries.title: De Notendop, the Tuesday duet with the Westertoren
entries.reason: Still there? (not known to have resumed after the tower's restoration)
entries.hook: A home-built music tub answers the carillon on trumpet; the carillonneur waves through a hatch in the clock.

entries.title: Hildo Krop's comic strip on the telephone exchange, Herengracht 295
entries.reason: Okay; panels' subject unknown, no second source
entries.hook: The city sculptor's 1957 relief on the PTD exchange, which the register says reads like a comic strip.

entries.title: Nine Streets, stones saved from demolitions
entries.reason: Okay; scout suggests a Look for line instead
entries.hook: Stones saved from houses pulled down in 1950, and the Oranjeappel orphanage gate.

entries.title: The garden house that travelled, Keizersgracht 62-64
entries.reason: Okay; not visible from the street
entries.hook: A 1699 garden house, dismantled in 1917, found overgrown in 1966 and rebuilt behind another canal house.

entries.title: Pottenbakkersgang, a path older than the canal belt
entries.hook: A pre-1612 path absorbed into the canal belt, still traceable between Herengracht 151 and 155.

entries.title: Langestraat 80, the Tsar in the gable and the Hollandsche Mediaeval
entries.reason: Okay; single source; next to "The tailors' saint" (no. 78)
entries.hook: Studio of the type designer of the Hollandsche Mediaeval; Stadsherstel's second restoration.

entries.title: The Fault in Our Stars bench, Leidsegracht
entries.reason: Okay; fan spot, thin on history
entries.hook: A film bench where young readers come to cry; stolen, replaced, still visited.

entries.title: Herenstraat 21, Meijer and Regina Turfkruier
entries.hook: Shopkeepers researched their house and had stumbling stones laid in 2026; inside, Regina's ring and purse.

entries.title: Waterline, the red climber on the Leliegracht quay
entries.reason: Okay; probably temporary; spot to fix on site
entries.hook: An unannounced red figure paints a waterline high on the quay wall, a climate warning since 2025.

entries.title: De Afstap, the wool shop that kept its name
entries.reason: Okay; single source; shop; number not printed
entries.hook: Fifty years of wool; knitted sixty fisherman's sweaters for Peter Grimes and a hundred for Soldaat van Oranje.

entries.title: Rien Bekkers's costume dolls, Herenstraat
entries.reason: Okay; Location and Still there? unknown
entries.hook: A costume designer's window of metre-high dolls in 18th-century court dress, changed regularly.

entries.title: Singel 390, the globe melted down and hoisted back
entries.hook: A copper celestial globe between Apollo and Minerva, melted for copper in 1914 and remade in 2002.

entries.title: De Vier Heemskinderen, four knights on one horse
entries.hook: A 1671 baker's stone at the corner where two city extensions meet: the four sons of Aymon on one horse.

entries.title: Centraal Station's two plaques: the cold welcome and the sergeant
entries.reason: Centraal Station is A-list: pitched on the plaques
entries.hook: A plaque admits the state "failed" the camp survivors it received here in 1945.

entries.title: Nieuwendijk 89, the photographer's front with Daguerre and Niépce
entries.reason: date of the front to confirm
entries.hook: A portrait photographer's front with putti taking pictures and medallions of the two inventors of photography.

entries.title: Sint Luciënsteeg, the gable stone wall
entries.reason: alley access during the museum rebuild
entries.hook: About 47 rescued gable stones on the museum's outer wall: a milkmaid, three moles, a skater.

entries.title: The neon HELP in the Voetboogstraat (Joes Kloppenburg)
entries.hook: Where a man died stopping a beating in 1997: a minute-by-minute plaque and HELP in neon overhead.

entries.title: Een zeegezicht aan het IJ, the tiled cycle tunnel
entries.reason: pitched on the art, not the station
entries.hook: 70,000 hand-painted tiles of a Rotterdam painter's herring fleet line the tunnel under the station.

entries.title: Rokin station: the archaeologists' wall and Manders' fountain
entries.hook: Thousands of metro-dig finds laid out by shape, not date; Queen Wilhelmina rides above on the Rokin.

entries.title: Annick van Hardeveld, the last courier
entries.hook: A 21-year-old courier shot on 4 May 1945 while the radio announced the surrender.

entries.title: Walk of Pride, queer names from the Dam to the Homomonument
entries.hook: Since July 2026 bronze-inlaid tiles with queer names run from the Dam to the Homomonument.

entries.title: Nieuwezijds Kolk, the castle under the street
entries.reason: no paving marker known; check on site
entries.hook: Foundations of a castle of about 1280, the city's oldest structure, found under the Kolk in 1994.

entries.title: Beurspassage, the "Amsterdam Oersoep"
entries.hook: A passage turned underwater canal: herring and bikes in the ceiling, bicycle-part chandeliers, a fish-head tap.

entries.title: The Dam shooting of 7 May 1945 and its 32 name stones
entries.reason: Dam is A-list: pitched on the stones; Victoria Hotel draft mentions the day
entries.hook: Name stones in the Dam's paving for those killed when Germans fired on the liberation crowd.

entries.title: Het Lieverdje and the words on the Spui
entries.hook: The little bronze boy where Provo began its happenings, with Lawrence Weiner's iron books in the paving.

entries.title: The last elm of the Stationsplein
entries.reason: station square is A-list: pitched on the tree
entries.hook: The sole survivor of 30 elms planted when the station was built, now ringed by young ones again.

entries.title: The bicycle garage under the water at Stationsplein
entries.reason: second source needed; panels' visibility unknown
entries.hook: 7,000 bikes nine metres under the water, with two 1965 sgraffito walls saved from a demolished institute.

entries.title: Art under Centraal Station: tomorrow's weather and a mosaic seen through peepholes
entries.hook: A screen landscape whose weather is tomorrow's forecast, and a granite mosaic glimpsed through peepholes.

entries.title: Canvas van Amsterdam on the Haringpakkersbrug, where the Haringpakkerstoren stood
entries.reason: Okay; changing work; gone tower (BC-03 lead)
entries.hook: A changing artwork on the bridge by the vanished herring packers' tower.

entries.title: Rokin 64, the Moor on the cornice
entries.reason: Okay; link to Bartholomeus de Moor unchecked; scout hint: group with Gouden Bril (AC-01)
entries.hook: A carved Moor on a cornice, used by Mapping Slavery to talk about colonial words.

entries.title: Hotel Polen fire, 1977
entries.reason: Okay; single source; no memorial found
entries.hook: 33 dead in the deadliest Dutch fire since the war; Rokin Plaza replaced the hotel.

entries.title: Olieslagerssteeg, leper house, oil pressers and Maison de Bonneterie
entries.hook: Oil pressers sold Haarlem oil as a cure-all here; a department store replaced the lepers' chapel in 1901.

entries.title: Oude Braak and the Nieuwezijds Armsteeg, the dike-arm lanes
entries.hook: Lanes on a dike breach and a curving dike arm, with the White Cube art space.

entries.title: Wijdesteeg, the mosaic alley
entries.hook: "They used to call this a filthy little alley": residents' mosaics in the Wijdesteeg.

entries.title: Vrankrijk
entries.hook: The squatted political club of the Spuistraat, still open.

entries.title: Kalverstraat 10, the booksellers' palace above the shops
entries.reason: Okay; or a Look for in "Look up in the Kalverstraat"
entries.hook: Minerva and Mercury above a shop window, where Rembrandt's print publisher kept shop from 1662.

entries.title: Het Veilinghuisje, the house everyone thought was demolished
entries.hook: A booksellers' auction house hidden in an inner court, believed demolished in 1989 and still standing.

entries.title: Blaauwlakenblok, the block the squatters held and the residents rebuilt
entries.hook: The Bijenkorf wanted it for offices; squatters held it; sixty houses restored with W139 and the Condomerie.

entries.title: The hole in the quay: a 600-year-old sluice under the Nieuwmarkt
entries.hook: A culvert runs under the Waag to a sluice paid for by a polder board 40 km away; fish hall and Bredero beside.

entries.title: The tallest tree in Amsterdam, Oudemanhuispoort courtyard
entries.reason: courtyard open weekdays only; or a Look for in the Oudemanhuispoort draft
entries.hook: A Dutch elm of 1890, 36 m tall and the thickest elm in the city, that thousands of students walk past.

entries.title: The red window of the Oude Kerk ("Het Rode Raam")
entries.reason: beside A-list Oude Kerk, pitched on the fight
entries.hook: One church window turned permanently red, lighting the nave from the Red Light District; heritage societies sued.

entries.title: Pijlsteeg, an alley through a hotel
entries.hook: One of the two streets where prostitution was allowed in 1413, now built over by Krasnapolsky but public.

entries.title: "GOD ROEPT U / JESUS LOVES YOU", the neon over the station square
entries.reason: the astronaut claim rests on the neighbourhood paper
entries.hook: The first words many arrivals read: blue neon on the old Hotel Karsten, said to be switched on by an astronaut.

entries.title: Belle and the bronze breast, Oudekerksplein
entries.reason: 1993 date and anonymity rest on blogs
entries.hook: The first statue of a sex worker, a groping bronze hand set into the paving, and the PIC next door.

entries.title: Trompettersteeg, the narrowest alley and its hidden coat of arms
entries.hook: Dopie's anamorphic city arms come right from one spot only; blacked out in anger, restored in 2021.

entries.title: Majoor Bosshardt on her bench
entries.hook: The Salvation Army officer of the Wallen sits on a bench drunk tourists would not leave alone.

entries.title: Chet Baker's window, Hotel Prins Hendrik
entries.hook: The trumpeter fell from a window here in 1988; fans put up an illegal trumpet pole, then a plaque.

entries.title: Koestraat, "Ons Dorp", the street with its own mayor
entries.hook: Residents crown a street mayor in Sweelinck's old garden; a 1912 stone for the inventor of the fire hose.

entries.title: He Hua temple and the Chinese Zeedijk
entries.hook: A Chinese Buddhist temple on the dike, "a striking stranger on the Zeedijk", with the Vesak procession.

entries.title: Bet van Beeren, 't Mandje and Hartjesdag on the Zeedijk
entries.hook: The café of Bet van Beeren, a bridge named after her, and the Zeedijk's revived drag street party.

entries.title: Mata Hari and the Determeyer skybridge
entries.hook: A uniform maker's 1929 bridge over the Korte Niezel, later the roof of an illegal gambling palace.

entries.title: Apotheek Van der Meulen, a pharmacy since 1696
entries.hook: Apothecaries on this corner without a break since 1696, the 1880 interior in its original blue.

entries.title: Spooksteeg, the ghost of the Zeedijk
entries.hook: Wailing nobody could trace drew crowds in 1853, and the alley was renamed Ghost Alley.

entries.title: Oudezijds Voorburgwal 61, four hundred years without piles
entries.hook: Stadsherstel found no piles at all: the walls stand straight on the ground.

entries.title: Geldersekade 78, the swindler Barmat
entries.hook: Home of the swindler Hitler used as a bogeyman in his propaganda.

entries.title: The murder of Magere Josje, 1957
entries.reason: Okay; single source; handle with care
entries.hook: A sex worker's murder in 1957 that young detective Baantjer never solved.

entries.title: Oudezijds Armsteeg "street gallery"
entries.reason: may be gone; pin not set
entries.hook: Residents turned a dumping corner into an open-air gallery of small vitrines in 2013.

entries.title: "Wandelend naar de Nieuwmarkt", the brick walkers on the Varkenssluis
entries.hook: Brick walkers of 1986, vandalised and remade in 2011 as four Chinese walkers with a lion dance.

entries.title: Bureau Warmoesstraat, the police station of Baantjer
entries.hook: Baantjer's police station, closed after a man put out on the pavement died; a plaque on the sandwich shop since 2025.

entries.title: Stoofbrug and the 3D-printed bridge
entries.hook: MX3D's printed steel bridge lay here two years; the lost old bridge was found and came back in 2024.

entries.title: Heintje Hoekssteeg, the alley that got its gate
entries.reason: Okay; beside A-list Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder
entries.hook: An alley used as a public toilet, now closed with a gate (2026).

entries.title: Jacob Hooy & Co., the drugstore of 1743
entries.hook: A herb and sweet shop with drawers and barrels unchanged since the 18th century.

entries.title: The Stopera, the NAP under it and the Violist
entries.reason: coordinator: re-source Kunstgebit, Schippers wedding room, before drafting
entries.hook: Town hall and opera fought as "Stop de opera"; inside, sea level as a bolt and an anonymous violinist in the floor.

entries.title: Nieuwmarkt metro station, the riot remembered underground
entries.hook: The station dug where the houses fell shows the 1975 riots in its art, and hides a 3,000-person Cold War shelter.

entries.title: Living by Numbers, the HIV/AIDS monument on the IJ
entries.reason: "first in Europe" is the makers' claim
entries.hook: Beads that counted toward 2030, the target for no new infections; called Europe's first HIV/AIDS monument.

entries.title: Megadlé Jethomim and the Monument Joods Verzet
entries.reason: one "memorials around the Stopera" pin possible
entries.hook: Paving traces an orphanage whose hundred boys and three carers went to Sobibor; beside it, Jews who fought back.

entries.title: De Dokwerker and the February Strike
entries.reason: on the Jewish Cultural Quarter square (statue itself not A-list)
entries.hook: Andriessen's docker for the 1941 strike; turned toward the synagogue in 1970 for the metro.

entries.title: The smoking skipper the city said no to
entries.hook: A twenty-metre skipper painted after the city refused permission; the canal shows through his coat.

entries.title: Where the Maupoleum stood: the "Colosseum", the green glass box and the tunnel
entries.hook: The ugliest building's successors got nicknames before they were finished; under the square, a motorway tunnel.

entries.title: Arcam's folded pavilion and the Museumhaven
entries.hook: An aluminium sculpture of an architecture centre, and twenty working boats that are lived in, not a museum.

entries.title: Nieuwmarkt square: the plane-tree fight, the paving-slab bird and the scaffold
entries.reason: the Waag is A-list: pitched on the square
entries.hook: Residents planted and fought over plane trees, a carver made a bird from a broken slab, the guillotine fell once here.

entries.title: The plaque for the Nieuwmarkt children, De Flesseman
entries.hook: Four neighbourhood boys shot in 1944-45, one two minutes after curfew; former residents put up the plaque in 1995.

entries.title: Vlooienburg under the Stopera: the plaque that took thirty years, and Spinoza
entries.reason: one Stopera pin possible with CC-04 / AC-23
entries.hook: The Jewish island under the city hall got a plaque for its murdered residents only in 2022; Spinoza stands outside.

entries.title: Lastage: the 1971 stone of nailed-up windows and the bridges for the neighbourhood's fighters
entries.hook: A gable stone shows the boarded-up Lastage of 1971; two bridges carry the names of the men who stopped the motorway.

entries.title: Leprozenpoort and the Grenspaal: the lepers' gate that moved, and a turtle carrying city debris
entries.hook: A lepers' gate with clapper-holding figures, rebuilt down the street; beside it a turtle carries scraps of demolished Amsterdam.

entries.title: Coentje Gans Plantsoen, a hidden garden for child victims of war
entries.hook: A gate that looks shut opens on a garden named for a boy of one murdered in Sobibor.

entries.title: Kalkmarkt 8, the seamen's doctor's pun stones
entries.hook: A port doctor named Voorsluis put a sluice on his house: "Exonerat et arcet".

entries.title: Valkenburgerstraat, shot after the surrender (5 May 1945)
entries.hook: After the capitulation German police stormed a building; four men who came to free the trapped were killed.

entries.title: The Tak family's six stones, Sint Antoniesbreestraat 98
entries.hook: Six stumbling stones for one household of the old Jewish quarter.

entries.title: A.S. Onderwijzerhof, a hofje from the 1980s
entries.hook: A hofje of the 1980s in the Nieuwmarkt quarter.

entries.title: OBA Oosterdok, the free view from the library roof
entries.hook: One of the few free high views of the old city, from the library that replaced the post tower.

entries.title: Speeltuin De Waag, a playground since 1932
entries.hook: A neighbourhood playground association on the same spot since 1932, still collecting old players' memories.

entries.title: The Marionettentheater in the old smithy
entries.reason: Okay; second source needed for the smithy meetings
entries.hook: A seventy-seat puppet theatre in the smithy where the Aktiegroep Nieuwmarkt met; a squatters' map of 200 addresses inside.

entries.title: Fort van Sjakoo, the bookshop from the squatters' years
entries.hook: An anarchist bookshop of 1977, born from the neighbourhood's resistance of the seventies.

entries.title: Huis Serne, a century of theatre costumes
entries.hook: Amateur actors ran a costume hire here from 1883; a ceiling painting ended a painter.

entries.title: Ruijtergaard, an orchard in crates
entries.hook: Pipes under the quay ruled out trees, so residents built a food forest in raised beds of city elm wood.

entries.title: Buurtpark 's-Gravenhekje
entries.hook: A residents' park on the old ramp to the rubbish barges, facing the Montelbaanstoren.

entries.title: Saint George and the dragon, Reguliersgracht 34
entries.reason: forging story needs a second source; private house
entries.hook: The relief's twelve faces are the twelve Jews hidden in this house; "I dive under to come up".

entries.title: Poentunnel, the bankers' tunnel under the Keizersgracht, and the Vijzelbank
entries.reason: nothing to see of the tunnel from the street
entries.hook: The only tunnel under a canal, dug so bank directors walked dry; the bank over the Kerkstraat caused a council storm.

entries.title: The krullen, Amsterdam's open-air urinals
entries.reason: three scouts proposed a krul (CW-04 Westermarkt, DC-40 Oudekerksplein): one pin, or one per zone
entries.hook: See-through iron urinals so police could count the men inside; Dolle Mina tied them shut in 1970.

entries.title: Four views of Den Helder, Kerkstraat 402-408
entries.hook: Four stones of 1672 show the coast a carpenter came from: Huisduinen, Den Helder, Nieuwe Diep, Wieringen.

entries.title: Orphan gable tops: the gables that played musical chairs
entries.reason: jordaan-5 draft has Rozenstraat 35-43: link or merge
entries.hook: About 135 canal houses wear tops taken from demolished houses; Prinsengracht 755's sea gods came from the Amstelstraat.

entries.title: Herengracht 412, perhaps the oldest garden house
entries.reason: private; garden houses were dropped at review as invisible from the street
entries.hook: A garden house crowned in 1734 whose core may still be 17th-century.

entries.title: Where Stichting 1940-1945 was founded, Keizersgracht 567
entries.hook: The resistance groups met here in secret in October 1944 to found their mutual-aid foundation.

entries.title: Herengracht 524, Jurriaan Andriessen's painted landscape room
entries.hook: Behind a neck gable, a whole room painted as a landscape in 1771.

entries.title: Hans Brinker Budget Hotel, proudly the worst
entries.hook: A hostel famous for advertising itself as the worst: guests leave in worse shape.

entries.title: Halvemaansteeg 4-6, the illegal demolition
entries.hook: An owner demolished listed houses without a permit in 2014; the gap is still there.

entries.title: Koningsplein 10, the 3-metre chocolate shop
entries.hook: An Art Nouveau front under three metres wide, built for a chocolatier in 1901 and rebuilt after a 1936 fire.

entries.title: The wall in the middle of the school, Weteringschans 263, and the children's resistance
entries.hook: A wall went up inside the school to split off the Jewish pupils; nearby, play equipment remembers their resistance.

entries.title: Speeltuin UJ Klaren, the first public playground in the country
entries.reason: "first" rests on Wikipedia: find the archive source
entries.hook: The country's first free public playground opened here on 8 May 1880.

entries.title: Frederiksplein: Van Hall's snapped tree and the Navalny memorial
entries.hook: A bronze tree broken over a wall for the banker of the resistance, and an informal Navalny memorial a student tends.

entries.title: Krop's monument for the Spieghelschool fire, Marnixstraat 404
entries.hook: The resistance burned the labour office in 1945; Krop's reprisal monument was stolen in 1967 and recast.

entries.title: "Tegen alle stromen in", Peter R. de Vries, Leidseplein
entries.reason: on an A-list square, monument is its own place
entries.hook: Two bronze hands gripping each other, with his life rules in 41 languages, steps from where he was shot.

entries.title: Zeelandbank, Weteringcircuit
entries.hook: A plaster stand-in waited a year before the real bench arrived with four Zeelanders in costume in 1958.

entries.title: Bureaucracy in Diversity, Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen
entries.hook: A Surinamese ballerina dances through a whirlwind of forms, after the childcare-benefits scandal.

entries.title: Ramses Shaffy, Levenslijnen, Vijzelgracht metro
entries.hook: A 24-metre LED portrait of the singer above the longest escalator in the Benelux.

entries.title: Max Euweplein: the prison where Anne Frank was held, now chess
entries.reason: De Balie draft already names the prison: split the story deliberately
entries.hook: The remand prison held the Frank family after their arrest; its square now hosts Euwe's chess museum.

entries.title: Pipe Museum, the world's smokes in a 1670 canal house
entries.hook: Over 30,000 pipes, from pre-Columbian to opium, in period rooms of a canal house.

entries.title: De Nederlandsche Bank: gold vault, garden, Zadkine and the lost glass palace
entries.hook: The bank opened its gold vault and garden in 2025, on the site of the Crystal Palace it replaced.

entries.title: Weteringplantsoen: the herb garden anyone may pick and the leaning poplar
entries.hook: Neighbours turned a dog lawn into a free herb garden; the city's biggest leaning tree leans over it.

entries.title: Blauw Jan's forty bronze lizards and De Kring
entries.reason: De Kring is a members' club
entries.hook: Forty bronze lizards crawl over a fenced lawn by the Leidseplein, beside the artists' club De Kring.

entries.title: Melkweg, the milk factory that became a hippie "cosmic centre"
entries.hook: A sugar refinery turned dairy turned youth centre in 1970, one hall for music, film and theatre.

entries.title: Stadsherstel's thank-you stones
entries.hook: Modern gable stones thanking Stadsherstel's people: a cyclist "tirelessly building bridges", golden wind feathers.

entries.title: Lange Leidsedwarsstraat 144, next to the inn "Het Land der Belofte"
entries.hook: A working-class house beside the vanished inn "The Promised Land" with its kolf course.

entries.title: Weteringschans 81-89, where the Grote Wetering squat fell
entries.reason: gone; or a paragraph in "Peper en Zout"
entries.hook: Riot police cleared the squat in 1980 and the city sent Sinterklaas along, which backfired.

entries.title: The robot car park under the Vijzelgracht and its poem cabins
entries.hook: Drivers leave their car in a glass cabin and a machine parks it under the canal.

entries.title: Leidse Dwarstuin, Lange Leidsedwarsstraat
entries.hook: A walled neighbourhood garden with a Bierenbroodspot mural in the tourist strip.

entries.title: The pagoda trees of the Falckstraat
entries.hook: The oldest Japanese pagoda tree in the city, a fern growing on it, flowering in August.

entries.title: The population register attack and the artists' resistance monument
entries.reason: building is part of the Artis complex: pitched on the street plaque
entries.hook: Artists and students set fire to the city's population register in 1943; Kneulman's monument stands round the corner.

entries.title: Weesperplein station: the Cold War shelter, its art and the Hortusbrug shelter
entries.hook: Fold-down tables, steel doors and a decontamination sluice for thousands; even a bridge nearby hides a shelter.

entries.title: Schaduwkade, the quay that remembers
entries.hook: The names of 200 deported Jewish residents line the quay opposite their homes; boats are now kept off.

entries.title: "Nooit meer Auschwitz", the broken-mirror monument, Wertheimpark
entries.reason: fairly well known; or group with Wertheim fountain
entries.hook: Wolkers' mirrors lie broken so the sky is never whole again; an urn of Auschwitz ashes beneath.

entries.title: The Brilleslijper house, Nieuwe Achtergracht 14
entries.reason: stone count to check on site
entries.hook: The resistance sisters deported on the Franks' train lived here; their family's stumbling stones lie at the door.

entries.title: Telefoon van de Wind, Hoftuin
entries.hook: A disconnected phone in a garden for calling the dead, after the wind phone of Otsuchi.

entries.title: CURACAO and PORTORICO, Nieuwe Keizersgracht 55-57
entries.reason: do not imply slave trade without a source
entries.hook: Two stones name Caribbean islands, and nobody knows why.

entries.title: Weesperstraat, the Jewish quarter's high street turned city motorway
entries.hook: The Jewish high street, emptied by deportation, was cut into a four-lane road; Krop's burghers watch from the blocks.

entries.title: Steven Holl's sponge on the Sarphatistraat
entries.reason: offices, outside only; Militair Hospitaal draft names the medicine store
entries.hook: Holl wrapped a pavilion in perforated copper beside the old state medicine store.

entries.title: Artisplein, Artis for free from a chair by the pond
entries.reason: Artis is A-list: pitched on the free square
entries.hook: Pull up a chair by the pond and watch the flamingos, without a ticket.

entries.title: Monument van Joodse Erkentelijkheid, the monument nobody wanted next door
entries.hook: The 1950 Jewish thank-you to Amsterdam, moved again and again, refused by one park's residents.

entries.title: The Stolperschwelle at the tram stop, Plantage Middenlaan
entries.hook: A stumbling threshold: tens of thousands deported from here by municipal tram.

entries.title: Wertheimpark's trees: IJzeren Hein and the dawn redwood
entries.hook: A wingnut held together with iron anchors, and one of the first dawn redwoods grown in the country.

entries.title: The elm museum round the Hortus: lying elms and an Anne Frank seedling
entries.hook: Elms planted lying down to replace the fallen ones, now curving upward; an Anne Frank chestnut seedling nearby.

entries.title: "De buurt borduurt", the embroidered wall, Weesperstraat 100
entries.hook: A 4 by 8 m embroidery stitched by 277 neighbours against the grey of the Weesperstraat.

entries.title: The Stolpersteine of the Nieuwe Prinsengracht
entries.hook: Twelve stones at no. 18 and eight at no. 50: whole households of the Weesperbuurt in one doorstep.

entries.title: The Stolpersteine of the Plantage Badlaan
entries.hook: A cluster of stumbling stones on the Plantage Badlaan.

entries.title: Nieuwe Kerkstraat, hidden synagogues and hofjes
entries.reason: Okay; thin sources, needs a gable check
entries.hook: A Portuguese-Jewish women's hofje, a Russian Jews' prayer house and a workhouse wall in one street.

entries.title: Plantage Muidergracht 1-23, a row restored by its own residents
entries.hook: Eleven owners restored their row house by house from 1993: "stadsherstel in eigen beheer".

entries.title: Weesperstaete, "De Doodskist"
entries.reason: Okay; or a Look for in Weesperflat / Diamantbeurs
entries.hook: Amsterdammers called Bodon's dark glass office "the coffin"; the committee refused its crown.

entries.title: Roeterseiland: the bridge building with its legs cut off, and Petit Versailles
entries.hook: The university cut four floors off a building to free the canal; residents saved a green courtyard from building.

entries.title: Professor Tulpplein, a professor who never was
entries.hook: Named after Rembrandt's Dr Tulp, who never held a chair; the houses on the old bastion sink.

entries.title: Mahatma Gandhi Plantsoen, the houseboat dweller's park
entries.hook: A houseboat dweller laid out this pocket park and put up the name board himself.

entries.title: Johnnyspot, the freerunners' square behind Carré
entries.hook: Low walls and level changes make this a top freerunning spot; neighbours complain of noise.

entries.title: Urban Jungle, Sarphatistraat 163
entries.hook: A life-size mural of a boy looking out to his future on a traffic strip.

entries.title: Hildo Krop's studio, Plantage Muidergracht 105
entries.reason: Okay; outcome and present state unknown
entries.hook: The city sculptor's old studio, fought over in 2016.

entries.title: The 120-year-old wisteria of Amstel 169-171
entries.hook: A wisteria so thick the city lists it as a protected tree.

entries.title: "Er ligt een roofstaat", the ship of the islands
entries.hook: A sculpted ship for the islands' yards, cut with Multatuli's line about a robber state.

entries.title: The floating gardens of Robert Jasper Grootveld, Wittenburgervaart
entries.hook: Three planted rafts in the provo's knotting technique, banned by the city in 2021, then given to the neighbourhood.

entries.title: Kattenburger Triomfboog
entries.hook: Twenty-five old Kattenburgers wrote their own history; their handwriting is fired onto the tiles of an arch.

entries.title: Mbulu Ngulu on the advertising column, Czaar Peterstraat
entries.hook: Since 1991 a West African reliquary guardian with purple rods sits on top of an advertising column.

entries.title: Jakoba Mulder's lamp, Mulderplein
entries.hook: A tilted disc, a leaf-cut lamp and nine chairs for one of the first women city planners.

entries.title: Kattenburg's fake old facades and the rent strike
entries.hook: The cleared island got a reconstructed gabled row; its tenants then held back rent for fifteen years and won.

entries.title: Het Funen, sixteen blocks by sixteen architects, and Lester's shards
entries.hook: A car-free park of sixteen blocks on five-sided tiles, with giant shards mapping the old bastion.

entries.title: The navy's firing range, now a roof garden facing NEMO
entries.hook: A windowless shooting range reopened in 2023 with a grandstand stair to a roof garden over the Oosterdok.

entries.title: Plukbos, the food forest behind the Wittenburg blocks
entries.hook: After three shootings a resident turned a dog field into a food forest open day and night.

entries.title: Shaffy's Tuin and the Shaffyboom
entries.hook: A garden named after Ramses Shaffy, and a maple that swallowed the railway fence, named for his 75th birthday.

entries.title: Hoogte Kadijk, the sea dike that still works

entries.hook: In 2023 the city shut its sluices and the old dike was the water barrier again; stones and a lost yard.

entries.title: Tkramrepus, the supermarket in reverse
entries.hook: "Supermarkt" backwards: you bring groceries instead of taking them; food-bank shoppers take free.

entries.title: Touwbaanpark, the 400-year fence and Waaigat 2

entries.title: The floating ball in the Oostenburgerpark

entries.title: Nieuwe Oostenburgerstraat, "het schattigste straatje"
entries.hook: Workers' houses of 1871 with postage-stamp gardens and benches under the kitchen windows.

entries.title: Tonia Stieltjesplein, Oostenburg
entries.hook: Residents named their new square after a Black trade-union woman of the 1920s.
